Guess what happens when an SSD dies? You can't write to it, but you can keep reading what's already on there. Don't trust sensitive equipment with moving parts and always backup whatever you can.

As someone in the IT trade, I feel obligated to mention that you are making it sound like you can trust them to do this.

A drive can fail for a lot of reasons. The thing you are specifically talking about is a feature of the drive that basically says "Stop allowing writes after X number of writes" which is to preserve it long enough to get data off it because the drive is past it's long term life expectancy.

What if it's controller pre-maturely fails? What if a chip on it is bad, causes a voltage spike as it ages, and fries some other chips?

In neither situation will the drive still be able to read the affected data.

It's a cool thing to know, but you shouldn't trust it is all I'm saying.

Backups are important. #1 IT Rule. Always have backups.

Welcome to the world of shortwave. In a nutshell, shortwave is a form of radio wave that can travel massive distances due to the way the waves bounce off the atmosphere.

Most of what you find are broadcast shows. News, religion, sports, pirate music radio. It's all there. In addition, you'll also find lots of amateur radio (HAMs) broadcasts of regular folks talking to each other. Lastly is the "oddity" stuff. Number stations. The Russian buzzer. Data stations. Crazy ramblings from anonymous people.

If there's a wild west left in this world, it's Shortwave. The hard part is finding a good radio and antenna to listen property. That website takes care of that part! It's still a lot more fun with your own equipment though

Heck, anyone can go out and get a HAM license and start DXing (Slang for trying to talk to other people long distances away via shortwave). like I said: The hard part is entry. A good radio can start around 100 bucks, and a good antenna, while fairly cheap, requires a lot of space to create.
